name: Standing Escape
description: Standing Escape starts on top in Invisible Collar. Clear the high head-and-arm clinch before recovering posture and foot posts to rise facing the guard.
summary: Standing Escape frees the top player's head and arm from Invisible Collar before they recover posture and rise to face the opponent's open guard.
overview:
The escaping player starts on top in Invisible Collar, with the bottom player's high leg-and-arm clinch controlling the head and an isolated arm. Standing requires freeing the head and arm, creating space and establishing a stable base. The facing high guard contains no rear hooks to remove.

The escaping top player faces a bottom guard player whose high legs control the head. One arm is isolated by the New York and neck-clearing sequence. Address the head-and-arm enclosure before rising; stop and tap if the neck or isolated arm is already loaded. Create slack at the opponent's hip and thigh before freeing the head and arm, without pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 134 Invisible Collar in Austin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCyIwacRKu8); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): What must open before you prepare to rise?
flashcards.answer: The top player must clear the opponent's high leg-and-arm enclosure before recovering posture and establishing a standing base.

plausible: Only second leg; first holds neck
Only hand grip; high leg curled
trap: Only overhook; legs still hold head

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): What should you do if the neck or isolated arm is loaded?
flashcards.answer: Stop the rise and tap so the partner releases the enclosure. Posture recovery must not force a captured neck or shoulder through the high guard.

plausible: Stand to pull your neck free
Twist the captured elbow outward
trap: Lift them before opening the loop

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): Where must space open before you free the head and arm?
flashcards.answer: Create slack at the opponent's hip and thigh while keeping your head aligned. Do not force the head upward or drag their foot against a fixed knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Space at their hip and thigh

plausible: At your head by pulling it upward
At their knee by wrenching the foot
trap: At your neck by turning it alone

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): What should you keep between you while creating distance?
flashcards.answer: Recover inside forearm frames as the head-and-arm enclosure opens. Keep the freed elbow near the ribs while separating from the high guard.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside frames and a compact elbow

plausible: Both arms extended outside the legs
A wide elbow behind their shoulder
trap: Hands on mat with head still caught

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): Which orientation helps you preserve that distance?
flashcards.answer: Keep your shoulders and hips facing the opponent while building a balanced standing base after the high clinch opens.
flashcards.answer_line: Face them while your hips move

plausible: Turn away with the arm still trapped
Twist head before shoulders can turn
trap: Face away while the high loop holds

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): When can supporting posts be established?
flashcards.answer: After the head and arm are clear, bring your feet underneath a balanced base before rising. Do not stand by lifting the partner through the high clinch.
flashcards.answer_line: After the head and arm are clear

plausible: While the high loop holds your neck
Before freeing the isolated arm
trap: As you lift them through the clinch

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): Why recover your freed elbow before rising?
flashcards.answer: A compact inside elbow makes it harder for the guard player to isolate the arm again while you establish foot posts. Clear the head-and-arm enclosure before standing.

plausible: Keep their high loop closed
Replace your standing foot posts
trap: Rise with your neck still captured

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): What does a stand-up need beyond opening the high legs?
flashcards.answer: Opening the high legs alone is not enough. Free the head and arm, recover posture and establish balanced foot posts before rising.
flashcards.answer_line: Clear head and arm; balanced posts

plausible: Only free hands, neck still caught
Only the second high leg opening
trap: Foot posts with the head restrained

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): The neck loop remains loaded as you start to rise; what now?
flashcards.answer: Stop rising and tap for a complete release. Do not lift or rotate your neck against the high leg-and-arm enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: Stop rising; tap for full release

plausible: Stand until the loop pulls apart
Keep rising with your arm trapped
trap: Turn your head against the high leg

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): What confirms readiness for the separate standing phase?
flashcards.answer: The high enclosure has opened, the head and arm are free, and balanced foot posts support your weight. Rise while facing the opponent's open guard.
flashcards.answer_line: Head and arm clear; feet support you

plausible: Second leg open, head still trapped
Hands free, isolated elbow caught
trap: Feet set, neck still under pressure

defender.name: Standing Escape Defender
defender.description: Standing Escape (defender): Use the remaining high leg and knee hug to control the opponent's posture when the second leg opens. Keep your high knee supported and the isolated arm contained without twisting the opponent's neck or shoulder.
defender.overview:
The escaping player starts on top in Invisible Collar, with the bottom player's high leg-and-arm clinch controlling the head and an isolated arm. Standing requires freeing the head and arm, creating space and establishing a stable base. The facing high guard contains no rear hooks to remove.

Use the remaining high leg and knee hug to control the opponent's posture when the second leg opens. Keep your high knee supported and the isolated arm contained without twisting the opponent's neck or shoulder. Keep the first high leg supported as the second leg opens, and release if the movement loads your knee or their neck.

If the second leg is opened, retain the neck-cleared knee hug only while it remains comfortable. Rebuild inside forearm and knee frames when the upper-body enclosure is lost. Release the whole enclosure immediately on a tap or loss of normal responsiveness; retaining guard never justifies loading a trapped neck.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Your high Invisible Collar enclosure can still apply vascular choke pressure during a posture change. Release promptly on any stop signal, and open the clinch if you are stacked or lifted. The top player beginning to stand does not make a trapped neck or your high knee safe to load.

Recover inside position: Rebuild inside forearm and knee frames when the upper-body enclosure is lost.

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): What can still hold their head as they start to rise?
flashcards.answer: Your high leg-and-arm clinch may remain closed as the top player changes posture. Recognize the remaining neck connection and release if it loads the neck or you are lifted.

plausible: Low knee frame after high legs drop
Loose ankle, thighs off shoulders

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): What supports your high leg while they free their arm?
flashcards.answer: Keep the high knee close and supported through your hip position. Do not hold the foot in place while the knee is forced away, or twist the opponent's trapped shoulder.
flashcards.answer_line: Supported knee with a free hip angle

plausible: Foot held while high knee drifts out
Ankle pulled against a fixed knee
trap: High leg straightened under a stack

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): Their neck is loaded as they try to rise; what must you do?
flashcards.answer: Release the whole high leg-and-arm enclosure on any stop signal. Do not retain the clinch through a forced rise, a stack or a lift.

plausible: Wait until they stand to release
Hold their head as they rise
trap: Open one hand but keep legs clamped

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): If only the second leg opens, what control may remain?
flashcards.answer: The neck-cleared first leg and knee hug can retain Chill Dog. Check that the remaining connection is comfortable; do not force a closed high clinch as the opponent regains posture.
flashcards.answer_line: First high leg with the knee hug

plausible: Rear hooks behind their hips
Both high legs already closed
trap: A knee hug after both legs disengage

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): Where should frames return if the high clinch is lost?
flashcards.answer: Bring the forearms and knees inside to keep a facing guard as the opponent creates standing distance. Recover guard structure rather than chasing a lost neck connection.

plausible: Both hands behind their shoulders
Knees outside as you chase the head
trap: Arms extended with the torso open
